name: Interpretation of biological patterns and trends

questions.q: How does an increase in temperature up to the optimum affect the rate of an enzyme-controlled reaction, and why?
a: Rate increases because thermal energy increases kinetic energy, leading to more frequent successful collisions between enzyme and substrate
Rate decreases because enzymes freeze solid
Rate stays constant because temperature has no effect on molecules
Rate drops to zero instantly due to denaturation

questions.q: What biological trend occurs to the rate of photosynthesis as light intensity increases from zero to a high level (assuming carbon dioxide and temperature are not limiting)?
a: Photosynthesis stops completely
Photosynthesis rate increases linearly until a saturation point (light saturation point) is reached where another factor becomes limiting
Photosynthesis rate decreases continuously
Photosynthesis fluctuates randomly up and down

questions.q: In a population growth curve of yeast in a closed culture vessel, what trend characterizes the stationary phase?
a: The population size decreases exponentially to zero
Birth rate is lower than death rate due to lack of food
Birth rate equals death rate as resources become limited, keeping total population size roughly constant
Growth rate accelerates rapidly without restriction

questions.q: What trend is observed in human breathing rate during strenuous physical exercise compared to resting state?
a: Breathing rate drops to zero to save oxygen
Breathing rate slows down and deepens
Breathing rate becomes irregular and stops periodically
Breathing rate increases in frequency and depth to take in more oxygen and expel excess carbon dioxide produced by respiring muscles

questions.q: When analyzing data on enzyme activity at 70°C, what major trend is typically observed, and what causes it?
a: Activity drops sharply to zero because high temperatures break bonds holding the enzyme's tertiary structure, denaturing the active site
Activity reaches an all-time maximum because molecules move infinitely fast
Activity remains perfectly stable indefinitely
Activity increases because boiling activates dormant genes

questions.q: What trend is expected in the mass of potato cylinders placed in a concentrated sucrose solution (high solute concentration) over 60 minutes?
a: Mass increases significantly as water enters by osmosis
Mass decreases because water molecules move out of the potato cells down a water potential gradient into the surrounding hypertonic solution
Mass remains absolutely unchanged
Potato cylinders dissolve into liquid completely

questions.q: How does increasing carbon dioxide concentration affect the rate of transpiration in a plant shoot under normal conditions?
a: It has no direct effect on transpiration, though high CO₂ can induce stomatal closure which reduces transpiration
It causes plant roots to burst
It increases transpiration exponentially by boiling water inside leaves
It turns xylem vessels into phloem tubes

questions.q: What trend is typically observed in oxygen consumption of a small mammal when ambient external temperature decreases significantly?
a: Oxygen consumption decreases because the animal hibernates instantly
Oxygen consumption drops to zero
Oxygen consumption stays flat
Oxygen consumption increases as the metabolic rate increases to generate more heat to maintain core body temperature

questions.q: In an ecological predator-prey relationship graph (such as lynx and snowshoe hare), what trend is observed in the population cycles?
a: Predator population peaks lag slightly behind prey population peaks in a regular cyclic oscillation
Predator and prey numbers stay completely flat forever
Prey populations peak after predators
Both populations crash to extinction simultaneously

questions.q: What general trend does surface area-to-volume ratio exhibit as an organism increases in physical size?
a: Surface area-to-volume ratio increases rapidly
Surface area-to-volume ratio decreases as an organism gets larger, making simple diffusion inadequate for internal transport
Surface area-to-volume ratio remains constant regardless of size
Volume decreases while surface area stays zero

questions.q: What trend occurs in enzyme activity when pH is altered far above or below its optimum pH level?
a: Enzymes work twice as fast
Enzymes convert into substrate molecules
Enzyme activity decreases and eventually stops because extreme pH alters ionic charges, disrupting bonds and denaturing the active site
Enzymes become permanently radioactive

questions.q: What trend is observed in the concentration of lactic acid in human blood immediately following a 100-meter sprint?
a: Lactic acid concentration drops to zero
Lactic acid disappears from the body instantly
Lactic acid level remains constant
Lactic acid concentration increases due to anaerobic respiration in muscles lacking sufficient oxygen

questions.q: How does an increase in wind speed affect the rate of transpiration in a leafy shoot, and why?
a: Rate increases because moving air sweeps away water vapor molecules accumulating around stomata, maintaining a steep water potential gradient
Rate decreases because wind freezes leaf cells
Rate stays completely unaffected by air movement
Rate stops because wind blows leaves off the stem

questions.q: What trend is observed in the rate of an enzyme-catalyzed reaction when the enzyme concentration is increased while substrate is in excess?
a: Rate drops to zero immediately
Rate increases linearly because more active sites are available to catalyze the conversion of substrate to product
Rate remains completely unchanged
Rate fluctuates randomly

questions.q: What trend occurs in the germination rate of barley seeds when temperature is increased from 5°C to 25°C?
a: Germination stops completely at all temperatures
Germination rate slows down due to freezing
Germination rate generally increases as enzyme activity (such as amylase mobilizing food reserves) increases with kinetic energy
Germination turns seeds into flowers instantly

questions.q: What trend is shown by the concentration of carbon dioxide in a greenhouse containing actively photosynthesizing tomato plants during bright daylight hours?
a: Carbon dioxide concentration increases rapidly
Carbon dioxide concentration stays at 50 percent
Carbon dioxide concentration fluctuates randomly
Carbon dioxide concentration decreases as plants absorb it for photosynthesis faster than they produce it by respiration

questions.q: When investigating osmosis in plant tissues, what trend is identified at the point where the percentage change in mass of a potato cylinder is zero?
a: The external solution has the same water potential as the cell sap inside the potato cells (isotonic point)
Water has stopped moving across membranes entirely forever
Potato cells have died
The sucrose solution is 100 percent pure water

questions.q: What trend is observed in the volume of oxygen gas produced by pondweed when the light source is moved further away?
a: Oxygen production increases exponentially
Oxygen production rate decreases because light intensity drops, reducing the light-dependent stage of photosynthesis
Oxygen production remains identical
Pondweed begins absorbing oxygen instead of releasing it

questions.q: How does human heart rate respond immediately after finishing a period of intense exercise, and what trend follows?
a: Heart rate stays elevated permanently
Heart rate drops to zero
Heart rate remains high initially to repay oxygen debt, then gradually decreases back to resting rate over a recovery period
Heart rate drops instantly within one second

questions.q: What trend is observed in soil nitrate concentration over time in a field where leguminous crops (like peas or beans) are grown and then plowed back into the soil?
a: Soil nitrate concentration drops to absolute zero
Soil becomes poisonous to all life
Soil nitrate level stays completely unchanged
Soil nitrate concentration increases due to nitrogen-fixing bacteria in root nodules and subsequent decomposition

questions.q: What trend is observed in enzyme activity when substrate concentration is increased from very low levels to very high levels (with fixed enzyme amount)?
a: Activity increases initially proportional to substrate, then flattens into a plateau when all enzyme active sites become saturated
Activity decreases continuously
Activity fluctuates erratically
Activity drops to zero immediately

questions.q: What is the primary trend in biodiversity as you move from tropical rainforests toward polar Arctic regions?
a: Biodiversity increases significantly in polar regions
Biodiversity decreases as environmental harshness and lower temperatures restrict species survival
Biodiversity remains perfectly uniform worldwide
Biodiversity drops to exactly one species globally

questions.q: How does humidity affect the rate of transpiration in plants, and what is the underlying reason?
a: High humidity increases transpiration because dry air pulls water out
High humidity stops photosynthesis
High humidity decreases transpiration rate because a high concentration of water vapor outside the leaf reduces the water potential gradient
High humidity turns leaves into roots

questions.q: What trend is observed in the electrical impulse frequency along a sensory neurone when the intensity of a skin touch stimulus is increased?
a: Impulse frequency drops to zero
Impulses travel backward toward the skin
Impulse speed increases to the speed of light
Impulse frequency (number of impulses per second) increases
